problem: LLM-based VLN models (Navid, NavGPT-2) encode every frame as dense visual tokens, which is costly. Egocentric views contain navigation-irrelevant regions (sky, distant background) and high-frame-rate sequences are temporally redundant, while generic VLM token pruning methods ignore these VLN-specific properties.
motivation: Real-time deployment of LLM-based VLN on embodied platforms is limited by prefill cost from large numbers of image tokens. Visually salient but navigation-irrelevant content and near-duplicate consecutive frames waste compute without helping navigation, so pruning designed for VLN should exploit depth (distance) and temporal similarity.
key_idea: Prune visual tokens jointly in space (attention-plus-depth importance score) and time (cosine-similarity frame dropping), then fine-tune the VLN model with a distortion-aware feature-alignment loss so pruned representations match full-token ones.
insight: Depth-aware plus content-aware scoring with fine-tuning retains most performance at aggressive sparsity, and the gap to ToMe/VisionZip widens as sparsity increases. For example, at 88.9% sparsity on Navid-CE R2R, SR is 34.9 vs VisionZip 32.6 and ToMe 28.3, and random pruning collapses to 0.0. No separate ablation of the spatial, temporal or distortion components is reported, so the individual contributions are not isolated.
method: Spatial-level token pruning: scores each patch as α·attention relevance (mean ViT MHSA attention) + (1-α)·1/(mean patch depth+ε) with α=0.5, and drops the lowest-scoring tokens
Diversity-aware filtering: keeps spatial coverage so entire regions are not pruned

Temporal-level sequence pruning: computes average-pooled global descriptors per frame and drops a frame if its cosine similarity to the previous frame exceeds τ; keeps keyframes with large motion difference or instruction shifts, and optionally adjusts τ using odometry
Distortion-aware fine-tuning: L_total = L_nav^pruned + λ·L_dist, where L_dist is the MSE between full-token and pruned-token features at M intermediate layers

Training setup: θp initialised from the pretrained full-token model; pruning modules and policy head are fine-tuned jointly; thresholds are updated periodically; Navid-CE recipe (oracle plus DAgger non-oracle trajectories) is followed

setting.backbone: Navid-CE (video LVLM, fine-tuned with pruning); NavGPT-2 FlanT5-XL/XXL (InstructBLIP, frozen ViT-g/14 and LLM)
setting.model_size: NavGPT-2 1.5B and 5B variants (FlanT5-XL 3B / XXL 11B LLMs); Navid-CE size not stated
setting.training_data: R2R train set (10,819 trajectories) plus Navid-CE oracle trajectories from 61 MP3D scenes and DAgger non-oracle rollouts; RxR evaluated zero-shot
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB sequence plus depth (RGB-D) used for the distance score
setting.action_space: low-level continuous actions in Habitat (Navid-CE); discrete nav-graph viewpoints for NavGPT-2 in MP3D
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE) and Matterport3D simulator; real-world tests on a Scout-Mini
setting.privileged: none (depth from RGB-D input; optional odometry)

numbers_note: Real-world results (Table 4, 77.8% sparsity; SR/NE per environment: meeting room 80%/1.64, bedroom 69%/2.07, office corridor 91%/0.99) are on in-house data and not included as a benchmark entry. 77.8% sparsity rows for the simulated benchmarks are also omitted. The paper's text labels the R2R table as VLN-CE, but the NavGPT-2 results are on the discrete R2R setting.
results: At 66.7% token pruning, STEP-Nav keeps over 95% of Navid-CE's performance on R2R-CE (SR 36.4 vs 37.4, SPL 35.3 vs 35.9). It beats ToMe and VisionZip at every sparsity level, e.g. at 88.9% on Navid-CE SR 34.9 vs 32.6 for VisionZip, and on NavGPT-2 XL SR 65.6 vs 64.2. Gains transfer to RxR-CE zero-shot and to a real robot, though on the 5B NavGPT-2 VisionZip has slightly higher SR and SPL (70.1/59.1 vs 69.6/58.4).
limitations: Only visual tokens are pruned; the textual branch is left as future work
No ablations isolating the spatial, temporal, or distortion-loss components, and no direct latency or FLOPs table is shown
Relies on depth input and fine-tuning for each base model; the distance score requires RGB-D and the temporal module has extra heuristics (keyframes, optional odometry)
